summary: Practise conflict-sensitive planning, partner controls, and adaptive reporting. Explore the five-day humanitarian project management course.
lede: Humanitarian project management in conflict zones involves planning and adapting aid delivery as needs, access, and partner conditions change. For humanitarian project managers and programme officers, the course covers conflict-sensitive and access analysis, sequencing activities into feasible workplans, and checking partner responsibilities and indicator data. Learners also practise handling community feedback and documenting adaptation decisions in concise progress reports.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who plan, coordinate, monitor, or support humanitarian projects affected by conflict, access constraints, and fast-changing response priorities.
modules: IASC Cluster Coordination and Partner Assurance
prerequisites: Working knowledge of project or programme delivery is expected. Familiarity with humanitarian response activities is useful. No coding or programming is required.
